narrative.overview: The page is a shipping document. Ibukun is the shipper; each project is a numbered container with its paperwork on a form-paper slip. Dock concrete ground, corrugated muted containers, one hi-vis highlighter for clickable actions. Square corners, 2px ink rules, hazard-stripe edges, soft long shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Dock-grey ground, ink rules, form paper for reading surfaces
Four corrugated container tones with stencilled IDs
Hazard-stripe edge under the bar and above contact
One highlighter: hi-vis yellow on clickable CTAs only
Interactive yard, skill chips, motion switch

rules.name: The One Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks a clickable call to action and nothing else. Containers use oxide and khaki, never orange or mustard.

rules.name: The Paper-for-Reading Rule
rules.body: Long text sits on form paper or dock grey in ink; container paints carry only short stencilled labels and titles.

rules.name: The Rationed Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono and stencil faces appear only on container IDs, dates, stack lines and route steps, never on body copy.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Loaded Rule
rules.body: A container rises only to signal it is the one on the bill.

dos: Do reserve #ffd200 for clickable calls to action (Email me, Send message).
Do outline every object in 2px ink and keep corners square.
Do put reading text on form paper (#ededE6) or dock grey.
Do give every container a stencilled IBKA ID and keep container text high-contrast: white on teal, oxide, slate; ink on khaki.
Do respect data-motion="off" for any new animation or transition.
Do style by class; CSS modules scope class names.
donts: Don't use yellow for decoration, headings, badges or non-clickable emphasis.
Don't introduce orange, mustard or additional container colours that compete with yellow.
Don't fall back to the name, tagline and card-grid portfolio layout.
Don't round corners or add blur, gradients as fills, or hard offset shadows.
Don't use mono or stencil faces for body copy.
Don't target ids from the CSS module (see caveats); use classes.
